bull_bear.body:
- Government of India holds 89.93% equity and has control over the company, and the President of India appoints all Directors to the Board
- Retains a 26% equity stake in MMTC-PAMP India Pvt. Ltd., a precious metals processing joint venture with PAMP Ventures SA, Switzerland, that pays a dividend to MMTC
- Holds a cash cushion from the 2022 divestment of its NINL joint venture, which funds statutory obligations, employees and administrative overheads
- The Gajendragad wind project runs under a 20-year Power Purchase Agreement signed in July 2007 and is described by management as running successfully
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Existential risk of closure — the Government sees no continuing requirement for MMTC — The Government is of the view that there is no requirement of MMTC as a central canalizing agency and that relevant Ministries/Departments can trade through their own PSUs or other agencies. A formal Government decision regarding closure of the Company is awaited, leaving the entity's continuation entirely dependent on an external decision it does not control.
- Business activity has been stopped by Government direction, leaving the company non-operative — MMTC has undertaken no business activity since April 2022 in pursuance of the direction of the Ministry of Commerce & Industry and Board approval, and the company describes itself as continuing as an almost 'non-operative' company. There was no trading income during 2025-26, and the Company states it has not carried out any business activity for the last three years.
- Extreme revenue concentration in a single small wind asset with a PPA expiring in March 2027 — Revenue from operations is only the wind mill operations in Karnataka, and 99.50% of turnover is Wind Energy Generation from the 15 MW Gajendragad project. The 20-year Power Purchase Agreement with HESCOM expires in March 2027 and renewal approval has not yet been obtained, so the sole operating revenue stream has a known expiry date.
- Dependence on non-operating income — interest on divestment proceeds and one JV dividend — Management states the interest income and dividend income from its JV company are the main source of income of MMTC presently, with profit mainly derived from profit on sale of investment, interest income and dividend received from the JV MMTC-PAMP. The Company must meet statutory obligations, employee costs and administrative overheads out of the finite pool of funds received from the 2022 NINL divestment.
- Liabilities including contingent liabilities exceed available cash balance — The Board explicitly cited this in declining to recommend any dividend for 2025-26, stating that MMTC's main cash inflow is from interest income and that liabilities including contingent exceed available cash balance — a solvency and liquidity constraint disclosed by the Board itself.
- Trapped and impaired investments across joint ventures and the subsidiary, with recovery uncertain — The Singapore subsidiary MMTC Transnational Pte Ltd is under a winding-up order with liquidators appointed and the matter under CBI investigation; NCLT ordered liquidation of Sical Iron Ore Terminal Ltd in June 2023 and MMTC's claim to the liquidator awaits a response; a winding-up application for Kandla Free Trade Warehousing is pending before NCLT; and the Haldia land refund from the Haldia Development Authority is still awaited with no action taken to date.
- Erosion of the workforce and unfilled Board and management positions — The manpower of the Company is reducing due to resignations, superannuation and VRS, with no fresh recruitments in MMTC. The position of Director (P) is vacant, and after the financial year end all Independent Directors, three of five Government Nominee Directors and two of four Functional Directors ceased to hold office, weakening Board and committee continuity.
- Forward-looking statements in the Annual Report may not be realised — The Cautionary Statement notes that statements describing the Company's objectives, expectations or anticipations may be forward-looking statements within the meaning of applicable laws and regulations, and that actual results may differ materially from the expectations.

business.body: MMTC was set up as a central canalizing agency for trade, but in pursuance of the direction of the Ministry of Commerce & Industry and approval of the Board, it stopped all trading activity from April 2022 and continues on a non-operating basis. Its only revenue from operations is the sale of wind power generated by its wind farm at Gajendragad in Karnataka to Hubli Electricity Company Limited (HESCOM). Its remaining economic interests are financial: interest income on funds received from the 2022 divestment of its NINL joint venture, and dividend income from its 26%-held joint venture MMTC-PAMP India Pvt. Ltd., which operates a precious metals processing facility.

business.body:
- MMTC Transnational Pte. Ltd. (MTPL), Singapore — subsidiary: Wholly owned foreign subsidiary engaged in commodity trading; under liquidation as per Singaporean laws, with Deloitte and Touche LLP Singapore appointed Joint & Several Liquidators following a winding-up order of the High Court of the Republic of Singapore; the matter is under investigation by CBI
- MMTC PAMP India Pvt. Ltd. — JV: Joint venture between MMTC Limited and PAMP Ventures SA, Switzerland, operating a precious metals processing facility; MMTC holds 26%
- Free Trade Warehousing Pvt. Ltd. (FTWPL) — JV: SPV established in 2004-05 with IL&FS on a 50:50 basis to promote Free Trade Warehousing Zones in India; promoters decided to exit the project. Its two wholly owned subsidiaries, Kandla Free Trade Warehousing Pvt. Ltd. and Haldia Free Trade Warehousing Pvt. Ltd., administered land banks at Kandla and Haldia; the Kandla land was surrendered in 2020 and a winding-up application for KFTWPL is pending before the NCLT, while the Haldia land was surrendered to the Haldia Development Authority
- Sical Iron Ore Terminal Limited (SIOTL) — JV: Joint venture for construction and operation of an iron ore terminal at Kamaraja Port, held MMTC 26%, SICAL Logistic Ltd 63% and L&T Infrastructure Development Projects Ltd 11%; commercial operations never commenced, MMTC's Board decided in Sept 2016 to exit, and NCLT ordered liquidation of SIOTL in June 2023
- MMTC Gitanjali Ltd. — JV: Joint venture in which MMTC holds 26%; financial statements have not been received from the joint venture company for the year ended 31.03.2026
- BSE Limited — related party: MMTC participated in the equity of the Currency Futures Exchange 'United Stock Exchange of India Ltd', which was merged with BSE Limited; MMTC presently holds equity shares in BSE and received a dividend during FY 2025-26
- Government of India and Central Public Sector Enterprises under its control — related party: The Government of India holds 89.93% equity and has control over the company; CPSEs in which the Government of India has control are related entities

outlook.body:
- Continue on a non-operating basis with no business activities, in pursuance of the direction of the Administrative Ministry (Ministry of Commerce & Industry) and the Board
- Meet statutory obligations to stock exchanges, employees and administrative overheads from the funds received from the 2022 divestment of the NINL joint venture, pending a formal Government decision on closure of the Company
- Continuously review potential areas of cost reduction and take steps to reduce avoidable expenses
- Generate income by renting out surplus office space available with MMTC
- Seek renewal of the Power Purchase Agreement with HESCOM and explore running the Gajendragad wind project for another 5-10 years beyond its March 2027 expiry
- Pursue recovery of investments stuck in joint ventures under insolvency, including a claim filed with the liquidator of Sical Iron Ore Terminal Limited and a refund claim on the Haldia land lease premium
- Seek exemption from signing an MOU with DPE through DoC, given no change in business activity or financial position
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: MMTC has no expansion programme. The Company has undertaken no business activity since April 2022 in pursuance of the direction of the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, and continues on a non-operating basis pending a formal Government decision on closure. Its only physical asset in operation is a 15 MW Wind Mill project with 25 Wind Energy Generators, set up in March 2007 at Gajendragad in Karnataka at a total cost of approximately Rs. 68.5 crores on 31 acres of land leased from the Karnataka State Government for 30 years; power is sold to Hubli Electricity Company Limited (HESCOM) under a 20-year Power Purchase Agreement signed in July 2007. That PPA expires in March 2027, and the Company is exploring possibilities for running the project for another 5-10 years and making efforts to obtain approval for its renewal. Elsewhere the direction is contraction rather than expansion: the Singapore subsidiary MMTC Transnational Pte Ltd is in liquidation, the Sical Iron Ore Terminal JV is under NCLT liquidation, the Kandla land was surrendered in 2020 with a winding-up application for Kandla Free Trade Warehousing pending before the NCLT, and the Haldia land was surrendered to the Haldia Development Authority. The Company is instead seeking cost reduction and income from renting out surplus office space.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- No trading income is expected while business activities remain stopped since April 2022 on the direction of the Ministry of Commerce & Industry; the company describes itself as almost 'non-operative'
- Interest income on funds parked in banks from the NINL divestment and dividend income from the JV MMTC-PAMP are the main sources of income presently
- The only revenue from operations is wind power sold from the Gajendragad wind farm in Karnataka
- Establishment costs are falling as manpower reduces through resignations, superannuation and VRS, with no fresh recruitments in MMTC
- India's real GDP growth is projected at 6.6% in 2026-27, slower than the prior year due to global challenges, with retail inflation expected to rise to 5.1% and the RBI expected to hold rates at 5.25%
- Global growth is estimated to have slowed to ~2.8-3.0% in 2025 from 3.3% in 2024, with tariff rates climbing to levels not seen in a century and Geo-Economic Fragmentation replacing globalization

- Retains a 26% equity stake in MMTC-PAMP India Pvt. Ltd., a precious metals processing joint venture with PAMP Ventures SA, Switzerland, that pays a dividend to MMTC
- Holds a cash cushion from the 2022 divestment of its NINL joint venture, which funds statutory obligations, employees and administrative overheads
- The Gajendragad wind project runs under a 20-year Power Purchase Agreement signed in July 2007 and is described by management as running successfully

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Existential risk of closure — the Government sees no continuing requirement for MMTC — The Government is of the view that there is no requirement of MMTC as a central canalizing agency and that relevant Ministries/Departments can trade through their own PSUs or other agencies. A formal Government decision regarding closure of the Company is awaited, leaving the entity's continuation entirely dependent on an external decision it does not control.
- Business activity has been stopped by Government direction, leaving the company non-operative — MMTC has undertaken no business activity since April 2022 in pursuance of the direction of the Ministry of Commerce & Industry and Board approval, and the company describes itself as continuing as an almost 'non-operative' company. There was no trading income during 2025-26, and the Company states it has not carried out any business activity for the last three years.
- Extreme revenue concentration in a single small wind asset with a PPA expiring in March 2027 — Revenue from operations is only the wind mill operations in Karnataka, and 99.50% of turnover is Wind Energy Generation from the 15 MW Gajendragad project. The 20-year Power Purchase Agreement with HESCOM expires in March 2027 and renewal approval has not yet been obtained, so the sole operating revenue stream has a known expiry date.
- Dependence on non-operating income — interest on divestment proceeds and one JV dividend — Management states the interest income and dividend income from its JV company are the main source of income of MMTC presently, with profit mainly derived from profit on sale of investment, interest income and dividend received from the JV MMTC-PAMP. The Company must meet statutory obligations, employee costs and administrative overheads out of the finite pool of funds received from the 2022 NINL divestment.
- Liabilities including contingent liabilities exceed available cash balance — The Board explicitly cited this in declining to recommend any dividend for 2025-26, stating that MMTC's main cash inflow is from interest income and that liabilities including contingent exceed available cash balance — a solvency and liquidity constraint disclosed by the Board itself.
- Trapped and impaired investments across joint ventures and the subsidiary, with recovery uncertain — The Singapore subsidiary MMTC Transnational Pte Ltd is under a winding-up order with liquidators appointed and the matter under CBI investigation; NCLT ordered liquidation of Sical Iron Ore Terminal Ltd in June 2023 and MMTC's claim to the liquidator awaits a response; a winding-up application for Kandla Free Trade Warehousing is pending before NCLT; and the Haldia land refund from the Haldia Development Authority is still awaited with no action taken to date.
- Erosion of the workforce and unfilled Board and management positions — The manpower of the Company is reducing due to resignations, superannuation and VRS, with no fresh recruitments in MMTC. The position of Director (P) is vacant, and after the financial year end all Independent Directors, three of five Government Nominee Directors and two of four Functional Directors ceased to hold office, weakening Board and committee continuity.
- Forward-looking statements in the Annual Report may not be realised — The Cautionary Statement notes that statements describing the Company's objectives, expectations or anticipations may be forward-looking statements within the meaning of applicable laws and regulations, and that actual results may differ materially from the expectations.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue on a non-operating basis with no business activities, in pursuance of the direction of the Administrative Ministry (Ministry of Commerce & Industry) and the Board
- Meet statutory obligations to stock exchanges, employees and administrative overheads from the funds received from the 2022 divestment of the NINL joint venture, pending a formal Government decision on closure of the Company
- Continuously review potential areas of cost reduction and take steps to reduce avoidable expenses
- Generate income by renting out surplus office space available with MMTC

hero.oneLiner: MMTC Limited is a Government of India central public sector trading enterprise that has ceased business activity and continues as an almost 'non-operative' company, with its only revenue now coming from a 15 MW wind farm in Karnataka.
